task_2.title: Disable wheel content validation during installation
task_2.description: Poetry 1.5.1 changes wheel installation so it no longer validates wheel file contents during RECORD validation. This avoids installation failures and resource issues on large wheels while preserving the existing handling for wheels that are still invalid under the remaining validation checks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing dependencies from wheel distributions does not fail or degrade because Poetry validates every wheel file's contents during installation, while still detecting wheels that remain invalid under the non-content validation rules.

expectation.grounded: During wheel installation, Poetry should continue to run wheel RECORD validation but skip validation of the actual archived file contents against that RECORD data. Wheels should only enter Poetry's invalid-wheel handling when the remaining RECORD validation still raises a wheel validation error.
expectation.conceptual: Installing a package from a wheel should no longer perform full content integrity checks that can make large wheel installs unreliable. Poetry should still recognize and handle genuinely invalid wheels when they fail the validation that remains enabled.

constraints.grounded: Keep the change scoped to wheel installation behavior. Do not remove wheel RECORD validation entirely, and do not stop tracking wheels as invalid when the reduced validation still detects an error.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should reduce unnecessary install-time validation work without broadly weakening invalid-wheel detection or changing unrelated dependency installation behavior.

behavior: Wheel installation skips validating wheel file contents against RECORD content entries during the pre-install validation step.
Wheel installation still performs the remaining RECORD validation before installing the wheel.
A wheel is only treated as invalid by Poetry's existing invalid-wheel path if the reduced validation still reports a wheel validation error.
Large wheels that were impacted by content-validation-related memory pressure can install without triggering that validation path.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry installs a dependency from a large, otherwise valid wheel, it should complete installation without performing full wheel content validation.
When a wheel would only fail because its archived file contents do not pass content validation against RECORD entries, Poetry should proceed with installation instead of rejecting it on that basis.
When a wheel still fails the remaining RECORD validation after content checks are disabled, Poetry should continue to treat that wheel as invalid.

task_3.title: Prevent incomplete wheel downloads from being cached
task_3.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes wheel download caching so incomplete or interrupted downloads do not leave behind partial wheel files in cache. Only fully downloaded wheels should become visible for later reuse.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that wheel downloads are cached only after they complete successfully, and that interrupted or failed downloads do not leave partially downloaded wheel files behind for later reuse.

expectation.grounded: The wheel download flow that uses `poetry.utils.helpers.download_file` should write the destination artifact atomically. A successful download should produce the expected wheel file at the destination, while an interrupted or failed download must not leave a partially written wheel cached at that destination.
expectation.conceptual: Package caching should only expose complete wheel files. If a wheel download does not finish, the cache should remain clean instead of retaining an incomplete artifact that could be mistaken for a valid package.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing successful-download behavior of `download_file` and its callers. The fix should change only the persistence and visibility of incomplete destination files, without requiring callers to change the download API or altering the normal outcome of completed downloads.
constraints.conceptual: Normal installs and successful downloads should behave as before. The change must only prevent corrupt or incomplete cached wheels from surviving failed downloads.

behavior: Completed wheel downloads become available at the cache destination only after the download finishes successfully.
If a wheel download is interrupted, aborted, or otherwise fails mid-transfer, no partial wheel file remains cached at the final destination.
A subsequent install or retry should not observe a leftover incomplete wheel from a prior failed download as a reusable cached artifact.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry finishes downloading a wheel successfully, it should store a usable wheel file in cache at the expected destination.
When a wheel download fails after some data has already been received, it should not leave a partially downloaded wheel in cache.
When the same wheel is requested again after a failed download, Poetry should not treat a leftover partial file as a valid cached wheel.

task_1.title: Speed up dependency resolution during heavy backtracking
task_1.description: Poetry 1.5.1 improves dependency resolution performance for install and update operations that trigger extensive backtracking, especially when conflicting packages have many available versions. The solver now preserves reusable cache state across backtracking boundaries instead of recomputing it from scratch, while keeping dependency selection behavior consistent with prior releases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution avoids severe slowdowns during conflict-heavy installs or updates with many backtracking steps, while preserving the same effective package selection behavior as before.

expectation.grounded: During version solving, `VersionSolver` should retain reusable `DependencyCache` entries and contradicted incompatibility tracking across backtracking, removing only data created at rolled-back decision levels. Dependency lookups must continue to return the same effective candidate set as before, including performing a fresh provider lookup when filtering cached results by a constraint yields no candidates so prerelease-only fallback behavior is preserved.
expectation.conceptual: Dependency resolution should reuse safe prior work when backing out failed decisions so conflict-heavy resolutions finish much faster, without changing the solver's visible outcome or its ability to consider prerelease candidates in fallback cases.

constraints.grounded: Do not fully reset solver caches on every backtrack when earlier decision levels remain valid. Do not change dependency eligibility semantics relative to previous behavior, including cases where prerelease versions may only appear after a fresh search when no non-prerelease candidates satisfy the constraint.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must be non-breaking: keep valid earlier solver knowledge, discard only rolled-back state, and preserve the same dependency resolution semantics, including edge cases around prerelease fallback.

behavior: Backtracking no longer wipes all cached dependency search results; candidate lists discovered at still-valid earlier decision levels remain reusable.
Backtracking no longer forgets all previously contradicted incompatibilities; only incompatibilities learned at rolled-back decision levels are removed.
Dependency searches during solver preference and package selection now use decision-level-aware cache state so repeated backtracking avoids redundant provider work.

When a cached package list filtered by the current dependency constraint produces no candidates, the solver performs a fresh provider search so fallback-only candidates, such as prereleases returned only on a fresh lookup, can still be considered.
acceptance_criteria: When an install or update encounters dependency conflicts that require repeated backtracking across many package versions, dependency resolution should avoid the severe repeated-work slowdown seen in 1.5.0 and complete using reused prior solver state.
When the solver backtracks from a deeper decision level to an earlier one, it should retain reusable dependency candidates and contradicted incompatibility knowledge from levels that remain active.
When cache entries were created only in rolled-back decision levels, they should no longer affect subsequent resolution after backtracking.

When a tighter dependency constraint leaves no candidates in cached results, the solver should perform a fresh lookup and preserve prior prerelease fallback semantics rather than incorrectly concluding that no candidates exist.
When resolving the same dependency graph before and after this optimization, the solver should preserve the effective resolution behavior while improving performance in high-backtracking scenarios.

task_4.title: Restore relative-path script execution in poetry run
task_4.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes a regression from 1.5.0 where `poetry run` stopped correctly executing scripts invoked through an explicit relative path such as `./script.py`. The update preserves the user-supplied relative command token while keeping normal virtual environment executable and pip resolution behavior intact.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry run` correctly executes scripts referenced with an explicit relative path, including cases where preserving a leading `./` is required for correct process invocation.

expectation.grounded: `poetry run` should preserve an explicitly relative executable argument such as `./foo.py` when building the command to execute. Command construction through `Env.get_command_from_bin()` must not normalize that argument into a bare filename, while `Env.python`, `Env.pip`, and pip fallback selection must continue to perform filesystem existence checks correctly.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run scripts via `poetry run` using explicit relative paths, and Poetry should execute the exact relative target they specified. This fix should restore the prior behavior without changing how ordinary environment-managed commands are resolved.

constraints.grounded: The fix is limited to preserving user-provided relative executable paths during command execution. Resolution of normal environment binaries, exposure of the environment Python path, and the logic that falls back to embedded pip when the environment pip executable is missing must remain behaviorally unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Only the broken handling of explicit relative script invocations should change. Existing command lookup and package-management behavior should continue to work the same way outside this regression fix.

behavior: `poetry run` preserves a user-supplied executable token that begins with `./` instead of collapsing it into a bare command name.
An explicitly relative script path is executed with relative-path subprocess semantics, allowing scripts in the current working directory to run correctly.
Normal virtual environment executable resolution continues to return usable filesystem paths for Python and pip-related operations.
Pip command selection continues to fall back to embedded pip only when the environment pip executable is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry run ./script.py`, Poetry should invoke `./script.py` as an explicit relative path and the script should execute from the current working directory if it is otherwise runnable.

When a user runs `poetry run` with a standard command name that does not rely on an explicit relative prefix, Poetry should continue resolving and running the environment-managed executable as before.
When Poetry determines how to run pip inside the environment, it should continue using the environment pip executable when present and only fall back to embedded pip when that executable is missing.
When Poetry exposes or uses the environment Python executable for command execution, it should continue behaving as a valid filesystem path.

task_5.title: Fix in-project virtualenv detection during dependency installation
task_5.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes incorrect handling of in-project virtual environments so dependency installation and environment discovery no longer treat a configured project environment as already available before its directory exists.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency installation in in-project virtual environments does not fail or skip environment setup because a project virtual environment is treated as existing before it has been created.

expectation.grounded: When `virtualenvs.in-project` is enabled, Poetry should target an in-project virtual environment without treating the project's `.venv` as available until that directory exists. Environment resolution and environment listing should reuse the project `.venv` only when it is present. If `virtualenvs.in-project` is unset, an existing project `.venv` should still be auto-detected. If `virtualenvs.in-project` is explicitly `false`, Poetry should not select the project `.venv`.
expectation.conceptual: Poetry should distinguish between a project being configured to use an in-project environment and that environment already existing. Installing dependencies should create or select a usable environment instead of assuming a missing project environment is ready, and environment discovery should only show project environments that actually exist.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress automatic reuse of an existing project `.venv` when `virtualenvs.in-project` is not explicitly configured. Do not override an explicit opt-out through `virtualenvs.in-project = false`. Do not return or list a project virtual environment for a missing `.venv` directory.
constraints.conceptual: Existing in-project environments should keep working, explicit opt-out should still be respected, and users should never see a missing project environment treated as if it already exists.

behavior: A configured in-project virtual environment is not considered present until the project's `.venv` directory exists.

Commands that resolve the active environment should not reuse a non-existent project `.venv`; they should continue with normal environment creation or selection so dependency installation can complete.
Environment discovery should include the project `.venv` only when the directory exists.
When in-project virtual environments are not explicitly configured, an existing project `.venv` remains auto-detected.
When in-project virtual environments are explicitly disabled, the project `.venv` is ignored even if the directory exists.
acceptance_criteria: When a project has `virtualenvs.in-project` enabled and no project `.venv` exists yet, running dependency installation should not assume the project environment already exists; it should create or otherwise resolve a usable environment and install dependencies.
When a project already has an in-project `.venv`, Poetry should resolve that environment for project operations.
When available environments are listed for a project, the project `.venv` should appear only if the directory exists.
When `virtualenvs.in-project` is unset and a project `.venv` exists, Poetry should still recognize and use that environment.
When `virtualenvs.in-project` is explicitly set to `false`, Poetry should not reuse the project `.venv`.

task_7.title: Restore dependency parsing for cached repository packages
task_7.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes a regression where repository package artifacts served from cache could be interpreted incorrectly, causing their declared dependencies to be missed during resolution. The update restores consistent metadata handling for cached and uncached artifacts so dependency resolution remains correct.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that repository packages resolved from cache are inspected as real package artifacts so their declared dependencies are not ignored during dependency resolution, locking, or installation.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry reads metadata for a repository package whose wheel or archive is already cached, it must obtain package information from the actual artifact content through the normal retrieval path rather than treating the cache entry itself as the package file. Cached and uncached artifacts should therefore yield the same dependency metadata and package information.
expectation.conceptual: Using a warm cache must not change package dependency discovery. A package fetched from cache should behave the same as a freshly fetched package, including contributing all of its declared dependencies to the resolved result.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer dependency metadata from raw HTTP cache container files. Preserve correctness for both cache hits and cache misses, and avoid misleading package-download output for cache-reused artifacts.
constraints.conceptual: Caching may improve performance, but it must never change dependency semantics or misrepresent what the tool is doing to the user.

behavior: Cached repository artifacts are no longer parsed from cache storage data as if they were wheel or source archive files.
Dependency metadata for cached packages is extracted through the same artifact-handling flow used for normal package retrieval.
Packages obtained from cache contribute their declared dependencies during resolution instead of being treated as if they had no dependencies.
Dependency inspection behavior remains consistent between the first fetch and subsequent runs that reuse cached repository artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry resolves or locks a package from a repository and the artifact is already cached, it should include that package's declared dependencies in the resolved dependency graph.
When the same package is processed once without cache and once with cache, the resulting dependency metadata should be equivalent.
When Poetry inspects a cached wheel or source distribution, it should read valid package metadata from the artifact content rather than from cache-wrapper data.

When a repository artifact is satisfied from cache, user-visible behavior should remain consistent with a normal successful fetch and should not misleadingly suggest that dependency information was unavailable.

task_6.title: Fix prerelease selection for transitive dependency resolution
task_6.description: Dependency resolution now correctly re-evaluates transitive dependency candidates when stricter constraints eliminate previously cached stable versions. This allows valid prerelease-only resolutions to be found instead of incorrectly failing with no solution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution succeeds when a transitive dependency can only be satisfied by a prerelease after constraints become stricter during solving, instead of incorrectly reporting that no valid version exists.

expectation.grounded: During version solving, if a dependency was cached under a broader constraint and a later or backtracked decision narrows that dependency so the cached eligible set becomes empty, `DependencyCache.search_for()` must re-query `Provider.search_for()` for that dependency. The solver must then allow matching prerelease versions to be considered for transitive dependencies when no non-prerelease versions satisfy the effective constraint, rather than ending in `SolveFailure` or `SolverProblemError` only because the cache retained earlier non-prerelease candidates.
expectation.conceptual: When dependency resolution tightens a transitive version requirement over time, Poetry should re-evaluate available versions using the final effective constraint. If only prerelease versions satisfy that transitive dependency, resolution should succeed with the prerelease candidate instead of failing as if no version were available.

constraints.grounded: Do not broaden prerelease selection beyond existing resolver rules: prerelease versions should still only be considered when explicitly requested or when no other eligible versions satisfy the constraint. Cache invalidation must preserve decision-level correctness across backtracking so stale candidate lists from rolled-back states do not affect later resolution outcomes.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve normal stable-version preference and only change the previously incorrect failure case. Resolution results should no longer depend on stale cache state, dependency evaluation order, or prior backtracking when a valid prerelease-only transitive solution exists.

behavior: If a cached dependency candidate list is filtered by a stricter constraint and becomes empty, the resolver must fetch candidates again instead of treating the dependency as unsatisfiable.
Re-evaluation of a dependency under a stricter effective constraint must be able to surface prerelease versions that were not returned for an earlier broader search.
When a transitive dependency is progressively constrained so that only a prerelease matches, version solving should select that prerelease and continue resolution successfully.
Cache entries associated with rolled-back decision levels must not suppress or contaminate later dependency searches after backtracking.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project where a transitive dependency is first seen under a broad constraint and later narrowed to a range with no stable matches but at least one prerelease match, when Poetry resolves dependencies, it should succeed and choose the matching prerelease version.

When the resolver revisits the same dependency after additional constraints are introduced, it should base the result on a fresh evaluation of the narrowed constraint rather than only on previously cached candidates.

Given dependency solving that backtracks across decision levels, when a valid prerelease-only transitive solution exists after backtracking, the final outcome should still be a successful resolution rather than a no-solution error.
When stable versions remain eligible for the effective constraint, the fix should not cause prerelease versions to be selected solely because the dependency was previously cached.

task_8.title: Honor explicit sources over direct-origin matches
task_8.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes dependency resolution so that a dependency with an explicit source is no longer treated as satisfied by an already selected direct-origin package solely because the versions match. When the direct-origin package is not a full match, resolution now continues through normal source lookup and can select the package from the declared source.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that a dependency declaring an explicit source is resolved from that source and is not incorrectly satisfied by a direct-origin dependency of the same package name just because the version matches. Ensure that when a remembered direct-origin package does not fully satisfy a dependency, normal package lookup still occurs instead of treating the dependency as already handled.

expectation.grounded: During dependency resolution, Poetry must only reuse a direct-origin package for a dependency when that package satisfies the dependency as a whole, rather than checking version compatibility alone. Dependencies that declare an explicit `source` must not be satisfied by a direct-origin package from another origin, and if the direct-origin package does not satisfy the dependency, Poetry should fall back to normal package discovery from configured sources.
expectation.conceptual: When the same package can come from a direct origin and from a named package source, Poetry should honor the user's declared source choice. A direct-origin package may be reused only when it is a true match for the dependency; otherwise Poetry should keep resolving the dependency from the appropriate source.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing behavior where a direct-origin package can satisfy a dependency if it fully matches that dependency. Do not regress normal source-based resolution: a non-matching direct-origin package must not block package lookup from repositories, including cases where the mismatch comes from explicit source selection or other dependency incompatibility.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve successful reuse of valid direct-origin dependencies, but never let an invalid direct-origin candidate override or suppress the correct package source. If the direct-origin candidate is not an acceptable match, resolution should continue normally instead of failing early or silently choosing the wrong artifact.

behavior: A stored direct-origin package is no longer selected based only on package name and version constraint compatibility.
A dependency with an explicit source is not satisfied by a direct-origin package from a different origin, even when the versions are compatible.
If a direct-origin package does not satisfy the dependency, Poetry continues repository or package-pool lookup and may resolve the dependency from the declared source.
If a direct-origin package does satisfy the full dependency, Poetry may still reuse it as the resolved package.
acceptance_criteria: When a project declares a package via a direct origin and also declares the same package with an explicit source, the explicit-source dependency should resolve from the named source rather than reusing the direct-origin package solely because the version matches.
When a remembered direct-origin package is incompatible with a dependency, Poetry should continue searching configured package sources instead of returning no candidate for that dependency.
When a direct-origin package fully satisfies a dependency that does not require a different source, Poetry should still be eligible for resolution.

task_9.title: Reduce memory usage when installing large wheels
task_9.description: Poetry 1.5.1 changes wheel installation to avoid the excessive memory usage caused by full wheel content validation on large packages. The installer keeps RECORD validation in a lighter mode so remaining wheel validation problems can still be tracked through the existing invalid-wheel flow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing large wheel distributions does not consume excessive memory while still detecting wheel validation problems that remain observable during installation.

expectation.grounded: During wheel installation, Poetry should validate the wheel RECORD without validating the contents of every wheel entry, so `WheelInstaller.install` no longer performs full content validation. If the lighter RECORD validation still raises `_WheelFileValidationError`, Poetry should continue to record that wheel through its existing invalid-wheel tracking behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Installing large wheel packages should use a lightweight validation path that avoids checking the contents of every packaged file, reducing memory consumption while still recognizing wheels whose RECORD data is invalid.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove wheel RECORD validation entirely or bypass the existing invalid-wheel handling path. The behavioral change is limited to skipping content verification during installation; other RECORD validation failures should still be surfaced through the current invalid-wheel mechanism.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should lower memory usage for large wheel installs without broadly weakening wheel validation beyond omitting the expensive content-checking step.

behavior: Wheel installation no longer performs full RECORD content validation for every file inside a wheel archive.
Installing large wheels should avoid the excessive memory consumption previously triggered by content validation during install.
Remaining RECORD validation failures should still be captured through Poetry's existing invalid-wheel reporting behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry installs a large wheel distribution, it should no longer exhibit the excessive memory growth caused by validating the contents of all files in the wheel.
When Poetry installs a valid wheel, it should still perform RECORD validation in a mode that skips per-file content verification.
When non-content RECORD validation detects a wheel problem, Poetry should continue to surface that wheel through its existing invalid-wheel handling behavior.

task_11.title: Fix recursive marker merging for multi-constraints
task_11.description: The 1.5.1 update fixes a regression in marker handling where combining multi-constraint markers could recurse indefinitely during dependency resolution. Intersections and unions of negative multi-constraints are now resolved directly so projects with complex conditional dependencies can lock or resolve without crashing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that marker handling can combine multi-constraint exclusions without entering endless recursion, so dependency resolution for projects with duplicate conditional dependencies continues normally instead of crashing.

expectation.grounded: When marker handling combines two `MultiConstraint` instances in `poetry.core.constraints.generic`, `MultiConstraint.intersect()` should produce a `MultiConstraint` containing the distinct negative constraints from both operands, and `MultiConstraint.union()` should produce a `MultiConstraint` containing only the negative constraints shared by both operands. These operations should terminate directly instead of delegating recursively between operands, so affected lock and resolution flows no longer raise `RecursionError` while simplifying markers.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry merges environment markers that each exclude multiple values, it should simplify them deterministically and continue dependency resolution rather than crashing. Projects that declare the same dependency under multiple platform or Python-version conditions should be able to resolve those marker combinations correctly.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing `MultiConstraint` behavior for combinations with a single `Constraint`, including idempotent handling of repeated constraints, conflict detection for opposite operators on the same value, and the existing negative-constraint semantics. The fix should not change unrelated constraint types or introduce new public marker forms.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to the recursion bug in multi-constraint marker merging and should not alter already-correct marker behavior outside that scenario. Marker simplification must remain logically equivalent to the dependency conditions users declared.

behavior: Intersecting one negative `MultiConstraint` with another now yields a single merged exclusion set that contains all distinct excluded values from both operands.
Unioning one negative `MultiConstraint` with another now yields the shared exclusion set that both operands have in common.
Marker handling no longer loops recursively when these `MultiConstraint` combinations are encountered during dependency resolution.
Affected dependency lock and solve operations now proceed to a normal resolution outcome or a normal dependency conflict instead of failing with a recursion crash during marker simplification.
acceptance_criteria: When dependency resolution needs to intersect two marker multi-constraints, it should complete without raising `RecursionError`.

When two negative multi-constraint markers are intersected, the resulting effective marker should include every distinct exclusion contributed by either operand without duplicating repeated exclusions.
When two negative multi-constraint markers are unioned, the resulting effective marker should preserve only the exclusions that are shared by both operands.

When a project contains duplicate dependencies with conditional markers that trigger multi-constraint marker merging during locking or solving, Poetry should return a normal solver result or a normal dependency conflict, but it should not crash in marker handling.

task_10.title: Honor explicit sources in mixed direct-origin dependency constraints
task_10.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes dependency resolution for multiple-constraint declarations that mix direct-origin dependencies with version-based requirements. A direct-origin package can still satisfy an ordinary version requirement for the same package, but it must no longer override a constraint that explicitly names a repository source. This prevents incorrect locking and installation outcomes when projects combine platform-specific direct artifacts with source-repository fallbacks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that multiple-constraint dependencies combining direct-origin artifacts and version-based requirements honor explicit repository sources, so a version-matching direct-origin package does not incorrectly replace or suppress a source-pinned dependency.

expectation.grounded: For dependencies declared with multiple constraints in Poetry, direct-origin entries using `git`, `url`, or `path` may satisfy a compatible requirement for the same package only when that requirement does not explicitly set `source`. If another constraint for that package specifies `source = "<repository>"`, Poetry must resolve that requirement from the named repository instead of treating the direct-origin package as an equivalent match. This behavior should be reflected in dependency solving, locking, and installation results.
expectation.conceptual: When a project mixes a direct artifact for one environment with a repository-backed fallback for another, Poetry should use the direct artifact only where no repository source is explicitly requested. If a dependency branch names a specific source, that package should come from that source and remain separately resolved.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing behavior where a compatible direct-origin dependency can satisfy an unsourced version requirement for the same package, including in multiple-constraint declarations with mutually exclusive markers. Do not allow a direct-origin package to satisfy a requirement when the version is incompatible or when an explicit source is part of the dependency definition.
constraints.conceptual: Keep valid fallback behavior for ordinary version constraints, but prevent packages from crossing source boundaries. The fix should only stop incorrect substitution of source-pinned requirements by direct-origin artifacts.

behavior: A direct-origin dependency declared via `git`, `url`, or `path` continues to satisfy a compatible requirement for the same package when that requirement has no explicit source.
A version requirement that explicitly names a repository source is no longer considered satisfied by a direct-origin package solely because the versions match.

For multiple-constraint dependencies that combine a direct-origin branch with an explicit-source branch, Poetry resolves and keeps the source-backed package as a separate dependency candidate instead of collapsing it into the direct-origin package.
If the available direct-origin package is incompatible with the declared requirement, Poetry falls back to repository resolution rather than short-circuiting on the direct-origin candidate.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency has one marker-specific `git`/`url`/`path` constraint and another marker-specific version constraint without `source`, Poetry should allow the direct-origin package to satisfy the unsourced version constraint if the version is compatible.

When a dependency has one marker-specific direct-origin constraint and another marker-specific version constraint with an explicit `source`, Poetry should resolve the source-constrained branch from that repository instead of treating the direct-origin package as the same dependency.

When locking a project that includes both a direct-origin branch and an explicit-source branch for the same package, the lock result should retain the repository-backed package needed for the explicit-source branch.
When installing for an environment that matches the explicit-source branch, Poetry should install the repository-backed package rather than the direct-origin artifact.
When the direct-origin package version does not satisfy the requested constraint, Poetry should continue searching repositories for a compatible package.

task_12.title: Correct wheel tags for build-script builds
task_12.description: This update fixes wheel filename tagging for projects that build non-universal wheels through a build script. When Poetry or poetry-core is running under a different Python interpreter than the one used for the project build, the generated wheel now reflects the target build interpreter and platform instead of Poetry's own runtime, preventing incorrectly labeled wheel artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that wheels built for projects with a build script are tagged for the actual build interpreter, ABI, and platform, even when the Poetry installation invoking the build is running under a different Python version or environment.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry build` or a PEP 517 wheel build produces a non-pure wheel because the project defines a build script, the wheel compatibility tag must be derived from the target build interpreter rather than from the Python executable currently running Poetry or `poetry-core`. If the backend is not executing inside that build environment, it should obtain the target interpreter's compatibility tags and use them for the wheel filename. Packages without a build script should continue to use the existing universal wheel tag behavior. If compatibility tags cannot be obtained from the target interpreter, the build should fail instead of emitting an incorrect wheel tag.
expectation.conceptual: Binary or otherwise environment-specific wheels must advertise compatibility with the Python version, ABI, and platform that actually built them. Running Poetry from a different Python installation must no longer cause a mismatched wheel name. Pure Python universal wheel behavior should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not change wheel tagging for packages that do not define a build script; they should continue to emit universal tags based on declared Python support. Do not derive a build-script wheel's compatibility tag from Poetry's own interpreter when it differs from the project's build interpreter. Preserve failure signaling when compatibility-tag discovery from the target interpreter is unsuccessful.
constraints.conceptual: Keep universal wheel output stable for packages that are still universally compatible, and avoid shipping platform-specific wheels with misleading compatibility labels. If compatibility cannot be determined reliably, fail the build rather than producing a questionable artifact.

behavior: Projects that define a build script now determine wheel compatibility tags from the interpreter used for the project build instead of automatically using the interpreter running Poetry.
When Poetry or poetry-core is invoked outside the build environment, the generated wheel tag reflects the actual target interpreter, ABI, and platform of that build environment.
Projects without a build script retain the prior universal wheel tagging behavior derived from declared Python-version support.
If the build backend cannot retrieve compatibility tags from the target build interpreter, wheel creation fails with an error rather than silently producing a wrongly tagged wheel.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project that defines a build script and is built in a Python 3.8 environment, when `poetry build` is invoked from a Poetry installation running under a different Python version, then the produced wheel filename should be tagged for Python 3.8 and the build platform rather than for Poetry's own interpreter.

Given a project that defines a build script, when the frontend runtime and target build interpreter differ, then the wheel should still advertise the target interpreter, ABI, and platform compatibility.
Given a project without a build script, when a wheel is built, then it should continue to use the existing universal wheel tag behavior instead of switching to interpreter-specific tags.

When the backend cannot determine compatibility tags from the target build interpreter, it should fail the build with an error instead of producing a wheel with a potentially incorrect compatibility tag.

task_13.title: Restore export directives for explicit package sources
task_13.description: This patch fixes `poetry export` so exported dependency files include the repository directives needed for packages that come from sources configured with `explicit` priority. The goal is to keep exports usable with private or custom package indexes without requiring manual edits.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry export` preserves the repository directives required for dependencies resolved from sources with priority `explicit`, so exported dependency files remain usable with private or custom indexes.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry export` generates a text-based dependency export, sources with priority `explicit` must be considered when deciding whether to emit repository header directives. If an exported dependency comes from an explicit HTTP-based source, the output should include the matching `--extra-index-url`, and plain-HTTP sources should also cause the corresponding `--trusted-host` to be present.
expectation.conceptual: Exports should carry forward the index and host configuration needed to install packages from explicit sources, instead of omitting those lines and forcing users to patch the generated file by hand.

constraints.grounded: The fix should be limited to missing repository directive generation for explicit sources. Existing dependency entries and behavior for non-explicit sources should remain intact, and repository directives should only be emitted for source URLs that actually participate in the export.
constraints.conceptual: This should be an additive compatibility fix: it should restore missing source metadata for affected exports without changing unrelated export behavior or adding unnecessary repository directives.

behavior: `poetry export` must no longer ignore repositories whose source priority is `explicit` when building exported repository directives.
If the export includes packages from an explicit extra index, the generated output must include the corresponding `--extra-index-url` entry.
If that explicit source is served over plain HTTP, the generated output must also include the corresponding `--trusted-host` entry.
Exports that rely on explicit sources should be usable as generated, without manual insertion of missing repository header lines.
acceptance_criteria: When a project resolves one or more packages from a source configured with priority `explicit`, running `poetry export` should include the matching extra index directive in the exported text output.
When that explicit source uses plain HTTP, the exported output should also include the matching trusted-host directive.

When exporting a project that depends on both normal sources and explicit sources, the generated file should preserve the repository directives needed for the explicit-source packages to be installable without manual edits.
When no explicit source is involved, existing export behavior for dependency lines and repository directives should remain unchanged.
